compare.topic: Council push to limit when SAPD contacts ICE

headlines.headline: Three council members try to limit SAPD contact with ICE
headlines.summary: Same proposal, four angles. News 4 leads with conflict and a public safety warning, the Report with momentum after Democratic wins, KSAT with the withdrawal, TPR with local pushback. Why compare: the verb a writer picks, split, follow, withdraw or push back, decides who looks in control.

headlines.headline: San Antonio council members split over proposed limits on SAPD contact with ICE
headlines.summary: Three San Antonio City Council members are requesting a special meeting to consider limiting when police contact federal immigration authorities, drawing opposition from Councilman Marc Whyte, who argues the changes could hurt public safety.

headlines.headline: San Antonio takes another look at police’s ICE policy, following Austin and Houston
headlines.summary: Three San Antonio council members want to limit SAPD contact with ICE, following moves in Houston and Austin after Democrats swept Texas elections.

headlines.headline: Councilmembers withdraw request for meeting on SAPD cooperation with ICE
headlines.summary: A request for a special meeting to discuss limitations on San Antonio Police officers’ cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has been withdrawn.

headlines.headline: How San Antonio and Bexar County are pushing back against ICE expansion
headlines.summary: San Antonio and Bexar County officials are pursuing lawsuits, policy changes and resolutions in response to an expanding federal immigration enforcement presence in the region.

breaking.headline: Girl on electric scooter killed in hit and run in northeast Bexar County
breaking.summary: The Bexar County Sheriff's Office is looking for the driver who hit and killed a girl riding an electric scooter around 8:20 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22, at W.T. Montgomery Road and Century Tree Drive. The driver fled. Investigators believe the vehicle is a 2011 to 2016 Ford F-250 or F-350 with front passenger side damage. The girl has not been publicly identified, and tips can go to BCSOTrafficHomicide@bexar.org, where anonymous tips are allowed.

refs.t: Girl on electric scooter killed in hit-and-run crash, deputies searching for driver
Girl riding electric scooter killed in hit-and-run; BCSO looking for driver

top.headline: Failed school tax votes mean 200,000 corrected tax bills
top.summary: Tax measures failed in Northside, San Antonio ISD, East Central and South San Antonio ISD, so October bills that assumed they would pass must be redone. About 200,000 Bexar County owners get corrected bills, posted online before Nov 30 and mailed around Dec 1. About 10,000 who already paid get refunds, averaging about $35 countywide. Bills are still due at the end of January.

refs.t: 200,000 corrected property tax bills are on their way following failed school finance measures in Bexar County
Seguin ISD tax rate election passes by 96 votes as most Texas school districts' measures fail

top.headline: UT clears the way for the city to buy Spurs arena land
top.summary: The UT System Board of Regents approved selling 13.59 acres at Hemisfair, the former Institute of Texan Cultures site, to the city. The price is undisclosed but cannot fall below appraised value, and City Manager Erik Walsh has estimated about $60 million from the Midtown TIRZ. The land can only be used for an arena built within 10 years of closing. The sale is expected to close in early 2027, and Council must approve the final contracts.

refs.t: UT clears path for City of San Antonio to purchase land for downtown Spurs arena
Four things to know about next steps for downtown Spurs arena

top.headline: SAWS is back to Stage 2 watering rules
top.summary: Rain and cooler weather lifted the Edwards Aquifer's 10 day average above the 640 foot Stage 3 trigger, so Stage 3 ended Monday, Nov 23. Sprinkler watering stays once a week on your day, 5 to 10 a.m. and 9 p.m. to midnight. Hand watering with a hose is allowed any time.

refs.t: Rising Aquifer Levels Prompts Return to Stage 2 Watering Rules
SAWS ends Stage 3 water restrictions

top.summary: ICE officers detained a 54 year old man, named by ICE as Edgar Mortera Ambrosio Jr., at the city owned Culebra Bulky Waste Collection Center on Thursday, Nov 19, and Councilman Ric Galvan is asking his son to contact his office to reunite the family. ICE says its Fugitive Operations Team tried to stop the vehicle and the driver pulled into the site, while Galvan says city staff and camera footage showed an unmarked vehicle stopping the family there and that neither the city nor SAPD took part. The surveillance footage has not been released, so where the stop began is disputed. ICE says he was convicted in 1990 and entered the country illegally in 1994, a timeline the San Antonio Current says ICE has not explained, so that history is ICE's claim and is not independently confirmed.

refs.t: ICE identifies San Antonio man detained during operation at city owned waste facility
ICE allegedly conducts operation at City of San Antonio-owned bulk waste collection facility
Councilman seeks to reconnect family after ICE detention at San Antonio waste site

top.headline: ICE arrest at a city waste site draws Councilman Galvan's response
45 apply to replace the retiring Bexar County manager
top.summary: The county received 45 applications before the window closed Tuesday. Commissioners unanimously named Deputy County Manager Thomas Guevara interim manager, even though David Smith stays through year end. Smith has held the job since it was created in 2011 and earns about $313,000. No selection timeline is set, and incoming Judge Ron Nirenberg has criticized the late process for limiting public input.

refs.t: 45 candidates compete for retiring Bexar County Manager David Smith's job
45 candidates compete for retiring Bexar County Manager David Smith's job

sports.summary: Victor Wembanyama had 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals in 32 minutes Saturday, his second 50 point game this season after 52 against Dallas on Nov 4. The win moved the Spurs to 14 and 3, tied for the NBA's best record.

refs.t: Wembanyama erupts for 50 points, 19 rebounds as Spurs crush Pelicans
Wembanyama makes history in 18 minutes, finishes game with 50 points

sports.title: Wembanyama scores 50 with 19 rebounds as Spurs rout Pelicans 114 to 91
UTSA football beats UAB 19 to 17 and stays atop the league
sports.summary: UTSA won 19 to 17 over UAB on Saturday, Nov 21, and remains atop the league standings, according to the school. The women's basketball team beat North Dakota State 52 to 50 the same day. The men's basketball team also beat Air Force, its second straight win, at the Military City Classic.

refs.t: Roadrunners remain atop league standings with 19-17 victory over UAB
UTSA tops North Dakota State, 52-50
UTSA flies past Air Force for second straight win

politics.summary: A council committee advanced a proposal for more public reporting on SAPD interactions with immigration authorities, with a full Council vote set for Dec 3. SAPD plans to begin expanded monthly reporting on Dec 1. Police figures show detainers for 54 of more than 42,000 arrests from January through October. The city is also suing over a planned 1,500 person detention facility on the East Side, with a status update due to a federal judge by Nov 30.

refs.t: How San Antonio and Bexar County are pushing back against ICE expansion

politics.title: City moves to publish more data on police contact with ICE

politics.summary: The May ordinance requires landlords with five or more properties to accept veterans paying with VASH or Section 8 vouchers, but it was softened from what the mayor and advocates wanted. Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones is asking the Planning and Community Development Committee to consider a six month pilot with no exemptions. Veterans describe units in less desirable areas, loopholes, delayed payments and extra inspections.

refs.t: Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones pushes to expand veteran housing eligibility

politics.title: Mayor wants a no exemptions veteran voucher pilot

politics.summary: District 1 Councilwoman Sukh Kaur filed a request for a no surprises construction policy after complaints about unexpected road work. Companies closing streets or sidewalks for more than a week would get a standard permit, share closures with navigation apps and send text alerts. Small businesses hit by closures over a month would get stakeholder meetings. Staff review comes first, then the governance committee in December or January.

refs.t: San Antonio councilwoman proposes requiring construction updates to be sent to your phone

politics.title: Councilwoman wants construction alerts texted to residents

politics.summary: Carlos Trevino is scheduled for April 6, Patrick Murphy, one of the Texas Seven, for April 7, and Joe Luna for May 3. Trevino and Luna were convicted in Bexar County, which has seven people on death row. Incoming District Attorney Luz Elena Chapa says she will not take the death penalty off the table.

refs.t: Three Texas executions scheduled for 2027 include two cases from Bexar County

politics.title: Three Texas executions set for 2027 tie back to Bexar County

politics.summary: Four community input committees each meet three times for the proposed 2027 to 2032 bond, which invests $442 million in everything but drainage. Meetings run 6 to 8:30 p.m. and stream on the city's YouTube channel. Final recommendations go to Council on Jan 20, and voters would see the bond in May.

refs.t: Join The 2027 Bond Conversation
City Council came together to shape 2027 bond valued at $442M plus $208M for flood control

politics.title: 2027 bond committees meet through Dec 17
City moves to take over a Hemisfair parcel for affordable housing
politics.summary: The city told Hemisfair's park leaders it will take over the ground lease of a three quarter acre parcel known as D5, on South Alamo Street beside the Monarch Hotel. Park leaders say the move could have major repercussions, while the city says housing discussions are very early. The park's leaders say Council approval is required. Separately, the $43 million GrayStreet project at 550 Market Street has pushed its construction start to January 2027.

refs.t: City eyes taking over key Hemisfair parcel for affordable housing development

politics.title: Incoming DA Luz Elena Chapa names her new top team
politics.summary: District Attorney elect Luz Elena Chapa announced hires Friday, Nov 20, including Ina Minjarez as first assistant and Amy Perry as chief administrative officer. Ben Robertson will lead the civil division, replacing Larry Roberson. Chapa campaigned on overhauling the office's management, and retiring DA Joe Gonzales gave his final address to Commissioners Court on Tuesday, Nov 17. Commissioners Court has already moved one Gonzales lieutenant out of her authority.

refs.t: Meet the new guard at the Bexar County District Attorney's office

artistry.headline: NIOSA organizers weigh a 2028 return at a new site
artistry.summary: The Conservation Society of San Antonio, which ran Night in Old San Antonio for more than 70 years, says it would like to bring NIOSA back in 2028. President Betty Bueche told the San Antonio Business Journal the group is still studying feasibility, including financing and organization, and no plans are final. The revival would likely not be held in La Villita, and no new site has been named. The society canceled the 2027 event in September and ended its La Villita agreement with the city in October.

refs.t: NIOSA organizers weigh resurrecting popular Fiesta event at a new site

artistry.summary: Centro San Antonio is expanding the one day shirt celebration to April 20 to 23, 2027, the same Fiesta dates NIOSA would have used. It will have three stages, vendors and food from 5 to 10 p.m. nightly. The move follows the Conservation Society's NIOSA pause and the city ending its La Villita lease. Part of the revenue will go toward preserving the historic village.

refs.t: Centro looks to fill void left by NIOSA pause with Guayabera Fest in 2027

artistry.title: Guayabera Fest takes over La Villita for four nights in April

artistry.summary: The Fiesta Flambeau Parade Association picked Saucedo, a 1995 Uvalde High School graduate, to lead the 79th parade, themed Cosmic Nights, A Universe of Lights. The parade runs Saturday, April 24, 2027, during Fiesta, April 15 to 25.

refs.t: Fiesta Flambeau Parade Association names NASA engineer as 2027 grand marshal
Fiesta San Antonio Commission 2026 27 Leadership

artistry.title: NASA engineer Luis Saucedo named 2027 Flambeau grand marshal

artistry.summary: The College of Education and Human Development now sits together in the Durango Building at the Downtown Campus for the first time. It enrolled nearly 1,700 students in fall 2025. A VIA shuttle runs the 15 miles between campuses, and student services are moving downtown over the next year.

refs.t: UT San Antonio expands downtown campus offerings with College of Education move

artistry.title: UT San Antonio moves its College of Education downtown

revolution.summary: Leaders unveiled a three block district in Prospect Hill with a chapel, a Plaza of the Immigrants and the Mercado Corazon del Pueblo. Former Mayor Henry Cisneros said it affirms immigrant contributions. Private donors paid for it. The San Antonio Report reports the mercado opens Saturday, Nov 28, at 2203 W. Commerce St., the chapel is expected in February, and the plaza within a year or more.

refs.t: New Sacred Heart Heritage District to honor immigrant history, community in San Antonio

revolution.title: Sacred Heart Heritage District honors West Side immigrants
Immigration court hearings move to Dilley, raising concerns for San Antonio families
revolution.summary: Some immigrant families who attended immigration court in San Antonio are now being ordered to appear at the Dilley detention center, about 75 miles south of the city. Families not in custody must travel to a detention facility, and hearings run Monday through Friday inside it. One hearing was moved up from 2028 to November 2026 with six days notice. A San Antonio pastor says about 40 of her congregants have been detained in two years.

refs.t: Immigration court hearings move to Dilley detention center, raising concerns for San Antonio families

revolution.title: Robert E. Lee sign to come down from downtown building
revolution.summary: The San Antonio Housing Trust is removing the giant neon sign from the 10 story Robert E. Lee building at 111 W. Travis St., which is being renamed the Emerald on Travis. The city granted administrative approval for the name and sign change, but the trust still needs approval from the Historic and Design Review Commission. The trust bought the building in 2025, and all apartments will be reserved for households earning under 60% of area median income. No removal date has been announced.

refs.t: Robert E. Lee signage at downtown San Antonio building to finally come down

community.headline: San Antonio Food Bank is halfway to its 4 million pound holiday goal
community.summary: The San Antonio Food Bank says its holiday drive has reached about half of a 4 million pound goal, and the drive runs through Nov 30. Every $1 donated provides 10 pounds of food. Nonperishable food can go to any Security Service Federal Credit Union branch or the red barrels at neighborhood H-E-B stores, and gifts can be made at safoodbank.org/food4sa.

refs.t: San Antonio Food Bank halfway to 4 million-pound holiday food donation goal

community.title: City offices and libraries close Thursday and Friday for Thanksgiving
community.summary: City Hall and most municipal offices are closed Thursday, Nov 26 and Friday, Nov 27, and reopen Monday, Nov 30. Curbside collection is skipped Thursday, Friday follows Thursday's routes and Saturday follows Friday's. All libraries, community and senior centers and Metro Health clinics are closed both days, while police, fire and EMS stay on duty. Parking is free at city garages, lots and meters Thursday, and at meters only on Friday.

refs.t: City Announces Thanksgiving Holiday Schedule of City Services

community.summary: Positive flu tests rose 55% in the first week of November, and about 20% of tests were positive versus roughly 2% a year earlier. Experts urge anyone unvaccinated to get a shot before Thanksgiving gatherings and travel, especially around older adults, pregnant women and people with weakened immune systems. Most insurance covers the shot, and uninsured people typically pay $25 to $130.

refs.t: San Antonio flu season is several weeks early, but there's still time to get the shot

community.title: Flu season arrives weeks early in Bexar County

community.summary: Commissioners unanimously approved the Senior Justice Assessment Center, which starts reviewing cases in December. It brings together Adult Protective Services, county public health, the Sheriff's Office and city police, fire and human services. The group meets weekly on cases involving residents 65 and older. It aims to fix the problem of several agencies meeting the same vulnerable person without anyone seeing the full picture.

refs.t: Bexar County clears way for multiagency elder abuse team

community.title: Bexar County creates a team to review elder abuse cases

community.summary: Volunteers with River Aid San Antonio cleaned a 2.5 mile stretch of Salado Creek on Nov 21, clearing debris from floods and the site's golf course past. Arboretum San Antonio bought the former Republic Golf Club in 2023. The 200 acre site is slated to open in January with weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

refs.t: Arboretum San Antonio plans major Salado Creek cleanup before public opening

community.title: Arboretum San Antonio targets a January 2027 opening

community.summary: News 4 asked for help finding Ledesma, last seen Saturday. Check the station's page for the latest details. News 4 was still asking for help finding her Monday morning.

refs.t: HELP US FIND: 16-year-old Karia Shay Ledesma last seen Saturday

community.title: Hunt for missing 16 year old Karia Shay Ledesma continues
Bexar County's Felony Veterans Treatment Court graduates a class of 12
community.summary: The two year program, established in 2017, held a graduation for 12 veterans on Nov 12. Judge Kristina Escalona of the 186th District Court presides. One graduate, Josh Allen, enlisted in 2008 and spent 15 months in jail before entering the program. His words, that if he was the only life they saved, they did, gave the story its title.

refs.t: 'If I was the only life they saved, they did': Inside Bexar County's Felony Veterans Treatment Court

community.title: US loses measles elimination status as Bexar kindergarten vaccine rate sits at 93.6%
community.summary: The Pan American Health Organization revoked U.S. measles elimination status, and Mexico and Bolivia also lost theirs. Bexar County's kindergarten MMR coverage for 2025 to 2026 is 93.6%, against 93.3% statewide. One Bexar school reported 43% and four others are below 75%. The San Antonio Report says county rates remain below herd immunity.

refs.t: U.S. loses measles elimination status as Bexar County vaccine rates remain below herd immunity

business.title: Spurs arena road funding still hinges on a TxDOT decision
business.summary: The city has proposed a $106 million package of traffic improvements at Durango and I-37 near the planned arena, with the city paying $21 million from a bond and TxDOT asked for $85 million. City Manager Erik Walsh said the city is still working through the state share with TxDOT, and the scaled back 2027 bond is too small to pay for the I-37 work alone. Spurs chief legal officer Bobby Perez said the team feels good about the project's direction. No date is set for a TxDOT decision.

refs.t: Questions remain surrounding new road construction as new Spurs arena moves forward

business.summary: San Antonio is installing rooftop and carport solar at libraries, fire stations and senior centers under a $30.8 million contract with Big Sun Solar. The project grew from 42 planned sites to 52, with 35 finished. It should save about $1.8 million a year and offset roughly 11% of electricity use at city buildings. Permitting and easement reviews pushed completion back, but the city says it is within budget.

refs.t: San Antonio's city solar program set to be completed in 2027

business.title: City solar program slips a year to the end of 2027

business.summary: The 1 million square foot lift and access equipment plant on Palo Alto Road is expected to open in April. JCB filed plans for $8 million more in buildings on its 400 acre site, with construction starting in January. The company is projected to employ 1,500 people within five years under a $13.7 million city incentive agreement. A separate $8 million dealership is planned to open in 2028.

refs.t: Manufacturer JCB plans $8M in additional projects at Southside plant still under construction

business.title: JCB nears opening of its $184 million Southside plant

business.summary: A nearly mile long tunnel will link Morgan's Hotel and Wonderland across the Inclusion Campus on the Northeast Side. The Prufrock 5 boring machine arrived Oct 14, and an anonymous private donor funds the project.

refs.t: Elon Musk's Boring Company to begin underground tunnel construction at Morgan's Wonderland

business.title: Boring Company starts a tunnel at Morgan's Wonderland

business.summary: The arena would seat 17,000 to 18,500 and include a 1,500 vehicle garage. A city study found downtown's problems go beyond parking, so no new Alamodome garage is recommended. Officials are leaning on a proposed bond with $34.2 million for roads and VIA's Green Line in April 2028.

refs.t: Downtown has enough parking for new Spurs arena, but transit and road upgrades will be key, say city officials

business.title: Downtown parking is enough for the Spurs arena, officials say
City launches a Buy Local Holiday Pass with prize drawing
business.summary: The City of San Antonio's Economic Development Department released the Buy Local Holiday Pass, a free digital pass listing locally owned shopping spots such as markets and retail hubs. Shoppers who check in at four participating locations before Dec 31 are entered in a drawing for a Buy Local gift pack. The pass grew out of a city survey this summer and is part of the year round Buy Local campaign.

refs.t: City program lets San Antonio shoppers win prizes for supporting small businesses

business.title: BermudAir adds nonstop flights from San Antonio to Belize City and Grand Cayman
business.summary: BermudAir, a new carrier at San Antonio International Airport, will fly nonstop to Belize City and Grand Cayman from May 20, 2027, through Sept 6. Flights run Thursdays and Sundays, with one way fares from $159 to Belize City and from $169 to Grand Cayman. The city's Aviation Department welcomed the new carrier. BermudAir committed to the routes through next year in exchange for exemptions from landing and departure fees, according to the Express-News as cited by the San Antonio Current.

refs.t: Nonstop flights from San Antonio to Belize City and Grand Cayman
San Antonio International waives landing and departure fees to gain two new Caribbean flights

schools.summary: The North East ISD board voted to close Montgomery, Dellview and Oak Grove elementaries to help close a $20 million deficit driven by falling enrollment. The district expects to save $4.06 million, and students will move to Windcrest, Colonial Hills and Regency Place. Attendance boundaries were adjusted for the receiving schools. Closures take effect next school year, with transition meetings planned and no layoffs at the affected campuses.

refs.t: NEISD board approves closing 3 elementary schools to cut budget deficit

schools.title: NEISD closes three elementary schools in a 4 to 3 vote

schools.summary: Christina Martinez resigned effective Nov 16. Applicants must live in District 6 and apply by 4:30 p.m. on Dec 3, in person at the SAISD administration building or online. The appointee serves until May 1, 2027.

refs.t: SAISD board opens applications for District 6 vacancy after trustee resigns

schools.title: SAISD opens District 6 seat after trustee resigns

schools.summary: Public schools are projected to lose more than 135,000 students to about 5.33 million, a 2.5% decline. Commissioner Mike Morath blames lower birth rates and migration, and warns of budget shortfalls and closures. Special education enrollment is rising to over 928,000.

refs.t: Largest enrollment drop in Texas' recorded history means challenges for public schools, Morath says

schools.title: Texas posts its largest enrollment drop on record

schools.summary: Rep. John Bucy filed House Bill 376 to fund schools by enrollment instead of attendance. He asks districts to delay closure decisions. South San ISD is weighing up to five closures that could save about $6 million after a local measure failed.

refs.t: Lawmaker says school districts should wait to close schools

schools.title: Lawmaker urges districts to hold off on closing schools

safety.headline: Man found with critical head injuries on a West Side road
safety.summary: A man in his 50s or 60s was found lying on the side of the road in the 3100 block of West Commerce Street, near Elmendorf Lake Park, just before 9 a.m. Tuesday. A San Antonio police park officer found him, and he was taken to a hospital in critical condition. Police have not said whether he was hit by a vehicle or assaulted, and no suspects or arrests have been reported.

refs.t: Man found with critical head injuries on side of West Side road, SAPD says

safety.title: Four men face capital murder charges in a 2020 San Antonio killing
safety.summary: Four men have been arrested on capital murder charges in the June 2020 killing of a San Antonio man whose body was found June 27, 2020, near Casias Road and Hildebrand. KSAT reports an arrest affidavit says the men planned a robbery and beat him. Those accounts are allegations and have not been proven. The Bexar County Medical Examiner's Office attributed the death to blunt force trauma with possible asphyxiation.

refs.t: Fourth suspect arrested in 2020 killing of San Antonio man, affidavit says

safety.title: Missing 18 year old Jessie Rankin has been found, FOX 29 reports
safety.summary: SAPD's Missing Persons Unit had issued an endangered missing alert for 18 year old Jessie Rankin, who was last seen around 9 p.m. Sunday near Spring Harvest and North Lake on the Northwest Side. FOX 29 updated its story early Tuesday to say she has been found. The report does not say who found her or when, and her condition has not been reported.

refs.t: 18-year-old Jessie Rankin has been found
MISSING TEEN: 18-year-old Jessie Rankin last seen on Sunday

safety.headline: Man shot downtown after refusing robbers' demands
safety.summary: A 30 year old man was shot several times around 1 a.m. Sunday in the 200 block of College Street near East Houston Street. He told police two men demanded his belongings, and he was taken to a hospital with wounds to the lower abdomen. His condition has not been released. The two men ran, no descriptions have been shared, and no arrests have been made.

refs.t: Man refuses robbers' demands, gets shot multiple times on downtown street
Man shot in attempted robbery downtown, police say

weather.title: Showers today, a cold Wednesday morning, and a light freeze possible by Thanksgiving morning
weather.summary: Light showers are expected this morning through early afternoon, with a San Antonio high near 53. Wednesday morning should reach the mid 30s in town, and areas away from the city center could see a light freeze. Thursday morning may run one or two degrees colder. The National Weather Service Freeze Warning runs from midnight Tuesday night to 9 a.m. Wednesday for the Hill Country and Edwards Plateau and does not list Bexar County.

refs.t: Hazards and forecast, updated Nov 23 5:26 p.m.
Arctic-like chill heading toward San Antonio, with possible snow flurries in Hill Country
Light showers today, then clearing & COLD Wednesday morning

memos.title: ICE meeting request withdrawn to strengthen the proposal
memos.summary: Castillo, McKee Rodriguez and Galvan asked Nov 6 for a special meeting on an ordinance, modeled on Houston, limiting when SAPD contacts ICE. They withdrew the request Nov 14 to revise and strengthen it. Attorney General Ken Paxton has since sued Houston over the policy that inspired it. A separate SAPD reporting proposal goes to the full Council Dec 3.

refs.t: San Antonio takes another look at police's ICE policy, following Austin and Houston
Councilmembers withdraw request for meeting on SAPD cooperation with ICE

memos.title: CCR asks for a no surprises construction policy
memos.summary: Councilwoman Sukh Kaur's request would require permits, navigation app updates and text alerts for closures lasting more than a week. It heads to staff review, then the governance committee.

refs.t: San Antonio councilwoman proposes requiring construction updates to be sent to your phone

memos.title: CCR asks the city to explore high speed rail to Austin
memos.summary: Councilwoman Marina Alderete Gavito filed a request to convene Bexar County, regional planners and I-35 cities and pool funding. It goes to a governance committee meeting, date not set.

refs.t: San Antonio councilwoman pushes for high-speed rail connection to Austin

events.title: Pearl Night Market
events.summary: Free market at Pearl, 303 Pearl Parkway, from 5 to 9 p.m. Wednesday. It is the last night in the season long series, with handmade crafts and food from local vendors. A Holiday Night Market series starts in December.

refs.t: San Antonio markets offer handmade gifts and an alternative to Black Friday consumerism

events.title: Esperanza Peace Market
events.summary: The 37th annual open air market at the Esperanza Peace and Justice Center, 922 San Pedro Ave., is free. Vendors come from San Antonio, Mexico, Guatemala and Colombia, with gifts focused on peace, justice and cultural preservation. Hours are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Friday and Saturday and noon to 6 p.m. Sunday.

refs.t: San Antonio markets offer handmade gifts and an alternative to Black Friday consumerism

events.title: Tobin Center Holiday Art Market
events.summary: Free market at the Tobin Center, 100 Auditorium Circle, with more than 80 local artisans selling home decor, baked goods and jewelry. It includes photos with Santa and a mechanical reindeer ride.

refs.t: San Antonio markets offer handmade gifts and an alternative to Black Friday consumerism

events.title: San Antonio Food Bank Turkey Trot 5K
events.summary: Starts at the Commander's House at H-E-B Arsenal, 622 S. Flores St. The race starts at 8:30 a.m. and the start line closes at 8:45 a.m.

items.h: 18 wheeler explosion on I 35 killed a local trucker, medical examiner says
items.summary: An 18 wheeler pulling an empty trailer hit a concrete wall near Judson Road on the southbound I-35 access road and exploded about 10 a.m. Friday, Nov 20, killing the driver. The medical examiner's office identified him as Joe Barrientes, 61, a local trucker who regularly drove between San Antonio and New Braunfels. Police say he was the only person in the truck, and investigators are still working to determine what caused the crash. A separate crash near Toepperwein the same morning sent a box truck driver to the hospital.

items.h: Vigil honors Southside ISD officer Christina Lozano
items.summary: Officer Christina Lozano, 47, assigned to Southside High School, died after a two vehicle crash Nov 15 near Loop 1604 and U.S. 281. Another district officer suffered six broken ribs and the pickup driver was hurt; both are out of the hospital. The Sheriff's Office is investigating and no cause has been released. Students and neighbors held a vigil Sunday.

items.h: Mayor asks to rewrite the city's state legislative agenda

items.h: Council gave $166 million in TIRZ money to zoo, gardens and arena land
items.summary: In September Council approved about $166 million in tax increment funding, extended the Midtown TIRZ to 2060, and set aside $60 million for the Spurs arena land. The zoo, botanical gardens and Brackenridge Park Conservancy each get $10 million over five years. The mayor and Councilman Jalen McKee Rodriguez voted no. An amendment asked staff to draft a plan that could shorten the Midtown zone and support affordable housing.

refs.t: Council takes aim at TIRZ while voting to give millions to zoo, botanical gardens, Brackenridge, Spurs arena and more

items.h: OSHA cuts H-E-B penalty to $49,650 after a second warehouse death
items.summary: OSHA is investigating the April death of Austin Lewis Flores, who was injured at H-E-B's Northeast Side warehouse and died four days later. The agency dropped seven of 10 cited violations, lowering the penalty from $80,388. He was the second worker to die at the facility in under six months, and the October 2025 case is still under review.

refs.t: H-E-B faces nearly $50K in penalties amid federal investigation into employee's death

items.h: Boys and Girls Clubs close two clubhouses
items.summary: The Southside clubhouse closed Sept 25 and the Eastside clubhouse paused operations through the school year, citing financial strain. Net income fell to about negative $1 million in 2025 after pandemic funds ended. Only the Southtown clubhouse remains, down from six in 2020, and a councilman proposed three months of emergency TIRZ funding.

items.h: A wetter winter is forecast, and resilience hubs are ready
items.summary: A strong El Nino points to a wetter than normal winter, with a chance of snow or freezing rain if Arctic air arrives. Residents are told to protect pipes and prepare emergency kits. The city can open libraries and community centers as resilience hubs, and people with medical needs can register with the state's emergency assistance registry.
